using ModelContextProtocol;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddMcpServer()
    .WithHttpTransport()
    .WithToolsFromAssembly()
    .WithResourcesFromAssembly();

var app = builder.Build();

app.MapMcp("/mcp");

app.Run();
```

### `ConfigResources.cs` — Resources

[McpServerResourceType]
public static class ConfigResources
{
    [McpServerResource(Name = "app-config", UriTemplate = "config://app")]
    [Description("Returns application configuration data")]
    public static string GetAppConfig() => /* JSON config */;

    [McpServerResource(Name = "env-config", UriTemplate = "config://environment/{env}")]
    [Description("Returns environment-specific configuration")]
    public static string GetEnvConfig(string env) => /* per-env config */;
}
```

### `Tools.cs` — Tools
```csharp
[McpServerToolType]
public static class MyTools
{
    [McpServerTool(Name = "echo"), Description("Echoes the input message back")]
    public static string Echo(string message) => $"Echo: {message}";

    [McpServerTool(Name = "add"), Description("Adds two numbers")]
    public static double Add(double a, double b) => a + b;
}
```

- **Packages**: `ModelContextProtocol` + `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore` (prerelease)
- **`WithHttpTransport()`** enables Streamable HTTP transport
- **`MapMcp("/mcp")`** maps the MCP endpoint (required string route pattern)
- **`WithResourcesFromAssembly()`** discovers `[McpServerResourceType]` classes
- **`WithToolsFromAssembly()`** discovers `[McpServerToolType]` classes
- Resources use `[McpServerResource(Name, UriTemplate)]`; parameterized templates like `{env}` become method parameters
